PetroEnergia Names Former Regulator as New CEO Amid Industry Optimism

PetroEnergia, one of Mexico’s largest independent oil and gas producers, announced the appointment of Ana Lucía Gómez as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective July 1. Gómez, 53, previously served as Deputy Commissioner at the National Hydrocarbons Commission, where she played a pivotal role in advancing Mexico’s upstream regulatory framework.

The company’s board of directors cited Gómez’s deep industry knowledge and regulatory expertise as key reasons for her selection. “Ana Lucía brings a unique perspective at a time when Mexico’s energy sector is evolving rapidly,” said board chair Hugo Márquez in a statement. “Her leadership will help us navigate both ongoing market opportunities and the complexities of the regulatory environment.”

Industry analysts view the appointment as a strategic move. “PetroEnergia is positioning itself to take advantage of the gradual liberalization in Mexico’s oil and gas sector,” said Mariana Aguilar, energy analyst at Mercado Insights. “Having a leader with government and technical experience is a significant asset.”

Gómez will succeed outgoing CEO Arturo Salazar, who is retiring after eight years at the helm. Under Salazar’s tenure, PetroEnergia increased its proven reserves by 18% and expanded its portfolio of onshore and offshore assets. The company’s latest annual report showed revenues of 19.4 billion pesos, with production averaging 48,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2023.

In her statement, Gómez said, “I am honored to join PetroEnergia at such a promising time for both the company and the sector. I look forward to working with our talented team to deliver sustainable growth and create value for all stakeholders.”

The Mexican Association of Hydrocarbon Producers welcomed the appointment, noting Gómez’s “commitment to responsible development.”
